answer: Reputation attested through stake-tiered verification can resist sybils: each agent deposits a bond to enter a shared trust terrace, where older and higher-stake participants get proportionally louder voting weight. Because identities must lock value before they can cast a signal in governance, creating thousands of fake accounts becomes expensive rather than free. A bridge of cross-chain attestations links identities across ledgers, so a sybil farm on one chain cannot cheaply re-spawn on another without leaving a traceable trail of duplicated stake patterns.
